M1013.name: Application Developer Guidance
M1013.description: Application Developer Guidance focuses on providing developers with the knowledge, tools, and best practices needed to write secure code, reduce vulnerabilities, and implement secure design principles.

M1015.name: Active Directory Configuration
M1015.description: Implement robust Active Directory (AD) configurations using group policies to secure user accounts, control access, and minimize the attack surface.

M1016.name: Vulnerability Scanning
M1016.description: Vulnerability scanning involves the automated or manual assessment of systems, applications, and networks to identify misconfigurations, unpatched software, or other security weaknesses.

M1017.name: User Training
M1017.description: User Training involves educating employees and contractors on recognizing, reporting, and preventing cyber threats that rely on human interaction, such as phishing, social engineering, and other manipulative techniques.

M1018.name: User Account Management
M1018.description: User Account Management involves implementing and enforcing policies for the lifecycle of user accounts, including creation, modification, and deactivation.

M1019.name: Threat Intelligence Program
M1019.description: A Threat Intelligence Program enables organizations to proactively identify, analyze, and act on cyber threats by leveraging internal and external data sources.

M1020.name: SSL/TLS Inspection
M1020.description: SSL/TLS inspection involves decrypting encrypted network traffic to examine its content for signs of malicious activity.

M1021.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
M1021.description: Restricting web-based content involves enforcing policies and technologies that limit access to potentially malicious websites, unsafe downloads, and unauthorized browser behaviors.

M1022.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
M1022.description: Restricting file and directory permissions involves setting access controls at the file system level to limit which users, groups, or processes can read, write, or execute files.

M1024.name: Restrict Registry Permissions
M1024.description: Restricting registry permissions involves configuring access control settings for sensitive registry keys and hives to ensure that only authorized users or processes can make modifications.

M1025.name: Privileged Process Integrity
M1025.description: Privileged Process Integrity focuses on defending highly privileged processes (e.g., system services, antivirus, or authentication processes) from tampering, injection, or compromise by adversaries.

M1026.name: Privileged Account Management
M1026.description: Privileged Account Management focuses on implementing policies, controls, and tools to securely manage privileged accounts (e.g., SYSTEM, root, or administrative accounts).

M1027.name: Password Policies
M1027.description: Set and enforce secure password policies for accounts to reduce the likelihood of unauthorized access.

M1028.name: Operating System Configuration
M1028.description: Operating System Configuration involves adjusting system settings and hardening the default configurations of an operating system (OS) to mitigate adversary exploitation and prevent abuse of system functionality.

M1029.name: Remote Data Storage
M1029.description: Remote Data Storage focuses on moving critical data, such as security logs and sensitive files, to secure, off-host locations to minimize unauthorized access, tampering, or destruction by adversaries.

M1030.name: Network Segmentation
M1030.description: Network segmentation involves dividing a network into smaller, isolated segments to control and limit the flow of traffic between devices, systems, and applications.

M1031.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
M1031.description: Use intrusion detection signatures to block traffic at network boundaries.

M1032.name: Multi-factor Authentication
M1032.description: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) enhances security by requiring users to provide at least two forms of verification to prove their identity before granting access.

M1033.name: Limit Software Installation
M1033.description: Prevent users or groups from installing unauthorized or unapproved software to reduce the risk of introducing malicious or vulnerable applications.

M1034.name: Limit Hardware Installation
M1034.description: Prevent unauthorized users or groups from installing or using hardware, such as external drives, peripheral devices, or unapproved internal hardware components, by enforcing hardware usage policies and technical controls.

M1035.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
M1035.description: Restrict access to network resources, such as file shares, remote systems, and services, to only those users, accounts, or systems with a legitimate business requirement.

M1036.name: Account Use Policies
M1036.description: Account Use Policies help mitigate unauthorized access by configuring and enforcing rules that govern how and when accounts can be used.

M1037.name: Filter Network Traffic
M1037.description: Employ network appliances and endpoint software to filter ingress, egress, and lateral network traffic.

M1038.name: Execution Prevention
M1038.description: Prevent the execution of unauthorized or malicious code on systems by implementing application control, script blocking, and other execution prevention mechanisms.

M1039.name: Environment Variable Permissions
M1039.description: Restrict the modification of environment variables to authorized users and processes by enforcing strict permissions and policies.

M1040.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
M1040.description: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint refers to the use of technologies and strategies to detect and block potentially malicious activities by analyzing the behavior of processes, files, API calls, and other endpoint events.

M1041.name: Encrypt Sensitive Information
M1041.description: Protect sensitive information at rest, in transit, and during processing by using strong encryption algorithms.

M1042.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
M1042.description: Disable or remove unnecessary and potentially vulnerable software, features, or services to reduce the attack surface and prevent abuse by adversaries.

M1043.name: Credential Access Protection
M1043.description: Credential Access Protection focuses on implementing measures to prevent adversaries from obtaining credentials, such as passwords, hashes, tokens, or keys, that could be used for unauthorized access.

M1044.name: Restrict Library Loading
M1044.description: Restricting library loading involves implementing security controls to ensure that only trusted and verified libraries (DLLs, shared objects, etc.) are loaded into processes.

M1045.name: Code Signing
M1045.description: Code Signing is a security process that ensures the authenticity and integrity of software by digitally signing executables, scripts, and other code artifacts.

M1046.name: Boot Integrity
M1046.description: Boot Integrity ensures that a system starts securely by verifying the integrity of its boot process, operating system, and associated components.

M1047.name: Audit
M1047.description: Auditing is the process of recording activity and systematically reviewing and analyzing the activity and system configurations.

M1048.name: Application Isolation and Sandboxing
M1048.description: Application Isolation and Sandboxing refers to the technique of restricting the execution of code to a controlled and isolated environment (e.g., a virtual environment, container, or sandbox).

M1049.name: Antivirus/Antimalware
M1049.description: Antivirus/Antimalware solutions utilize signatures, heuristics, and behavioral analysis to detect, block, and remediate malicious software, including viruses, trojans, ransomware, and spyware.

M1050.name: Exploit Protection
M1050.description: Deploy capabilities that detect, block, and mitigate conditions indicative of software exploits.

M1051.name: Update Software
M1051.description: Software updates ensure systems are protected against known vulnerabilities by applying patches and upgrades provided by vendors.

M1052.name: User Account Control
M1052.description: User Account Control (UAC) is a security feature in Microsoft Windows that prevents unauthorized changes to the operating system.

M1053.name: Data Backup
M1053.description: Data Backup involves taking and securely storing backups of data from end-user systems and critical servers.

M1054.name: Software Configuration
M1054.description: Software configuration refers to making security-focused adjustments to the settings of applications, middleware, databases, or other software to mitigate potential threats.

M1055.name: Do Not Mitigate
M1055.description: The Do Not Mitigate category highlights scenarios where attempting to mitigate a specific technique may inadvertently increase the organization's security risk or operational instability.

M1056.name: Pre-compromise
M1056.description: Pre-compromise mitigations involve proactive measures and defenses implemented to prevent adversaries from successfully identifying and exploiting weaknesses during the Reconnaissance and Resource Development phases of an attack.

M1057.name: Data Loss Prevention
M1057.description: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) involves implementing strategies and technologies to identify, categorize, monitor, and control the movement of sensitive data within an organization.

M1060.name: Out-of-Band Communications Channel
M1060.description: Establish secure out-of-band communication channels to ensure the continuity of critical communications during security incidents, data integrity attacks, or in-network communication failures.
